title: Zero-Shot Weight-Space Programming for Prediction and Classification of Target Variables in Structured Datasets

target_networks.name: linear (single affine map) and mlp8 (one hidden layer of 8 ReLU units) on tabular inputs

tasks_benchmarks: nine rotated synthetic rungs (s1_sep to s5_spiral, r1_lin to r4_sine)

headline_result.text: Claude Opus 5, shown a small table in context and writing every weight of a frozen network with no code execution or evaluation, matched closed-form optima on linear rungs and reached the irreducible error on three nonlinear rungs (e.g. 1.0000 on the parity rung vs 0.9662 for the same gradient-trained architecture), but failed on two oblique rungs (0.5084 on r2_kink, 0.5750 on s5_spiral).
headline_result.quote: The frozen network matches the closed-form optimum wherever that optimum is linear, reaches the irreducible error of the generating process on three rungs where it is not, and beats every fitted baseline on two of those

evidence_quality.n_runs_or_seeds: single (one sealed construction per rung and architecture; baselines over 20 seeds)

key_claims.claim: On the parity rung the hand-written network classified all 120 held-out rows correctly, above the Bayes rate and the gradient-trained network of the same architecture.
key_claims.quote: The result classifies all one hundred and twenty held-out rows correctly, above the Bayes rate of 0.9877 estimated on four hundred thousand fresh rows, and above every baseline including the trained network of identical architecture, which reached 0.9662.

key_claims.claim: Two constructions failed because the needed structure was oblique to the coordinates analysed; on r2_kink the construction reached 0.5084 against 0.8594 for the trained network.
key_claims.quote: A procedure that reads one feature at a time cannot see an oblique fold, and this is the rung on which that limitation is fatal.

key_claims.claim: On the real concrete regression the construction scored R2 0.7444 versus 0.7892 for gradient descent and 0.8749 for gradient-boosted trees.
key_claims.quote: The construction scores 0.7444 against 0.7892 for the same architecture trained by gradient descent, 0.8749 for gradient-boosted trees, 0.8096 for a random forest and 0.5697 for ordinary least squares.

key_claims.claim: Across four constructors, Sonnet 5 delivered nothing on three rungs and Haiku 4.5 wrote networks worse than predicting the mean while forecasting good scores; Grok 4.7 solved the oblique hinge rung that Opus failed.
key_claims.quote: The honest summary is that one of the two diagnosed failures is now known to be avoidable and the other is probably avoidable.

key_claims.claim: None of five 4-bit open-weight models from 0.49B to 8B delivered even the easiest rung.
key_claims.quote: No arm reached a second rung. All five stopped on toy_line, which asks for a line through twenty rows of one feature

key_claims.claim: The training error of a linear separator, not the composite complexity index, predicts what the hidden layer adds.
key_claims.quote: What predicts whether the hidden layer earns its keep is the training error of a linear separator, which the composite complexity index fails to track.

limitations_stated.text: One partition per rung, so small differences should not be read.
limitations_stated.quote: There is one partition per rung, so the binomial noise on a classification score of a hundred and twenty held-out rows is about four and a half points at ninety-five per cent confidence

limitations_stated.text: The synthetic rungs were generated by the same model that wrote the constructions, which knows each rung's qualitative family.
limitations_stated.quote: The synthetic rungs were generated by the same model that wrote the constructions, which knows the qualitative family of each one

limitations_stated.text: The Opus arm was written by the session that authored the generating processes and was less isolated than the other arms.
limitations_stated.quote: The Opus arm reported in the preceding subsections was written by the same session that had authored the generating processes, and it was trusted not to consult them.

notes_for_review: Extends WSP from compiling known rules to statistical inference: the LLM writes all weights of a tiny MLP from an in-context table with no code execution and no evaluation, under sealed digests and self-declared score predictions. Results are strong on toy and named-structure synthetic problems and competitive on classical tables, but each construction is a single pass on one partition, networks are very small (at most 8 hidden units), and the main Opus arm was not isolated from the generating code. A useful detail for the review is the failure taxonomy (non-delivery, confident bad networks, inadmissible code) and the finding that no open-weight model up to 8B (4-bit) can deliver even a line fit.
